newsitem.title: CHINA: China nabs six officials for stealing from poor.
newsitem.headline: China nabs six officials for stealing from poor.

text.p: Authorities in China's northern Shaanxi province have arrested six officials for stealing 11 million yuan ($1.3 million) from the poor, the People's Daily said on Monday.

The six, including Jin Jianhui, director of the provincial department of civil affairs, and his two deputies, had allegedly been embezzling and helping themselves to illegal loans from poverty relief funds since 1992, the newspaper said.
They also accepted bribes totalling 700,000 yuan ($84,000), it said. It did not say when the group was arrested or how the scandal came to light.
If indicted and convicted, the suspects could be sentenced to death.
A seventh suspect has been released on bail, the newspaper said. Five other officials were under investigation for alleged involvement in the scandal.
It was Shaanxi's biggest corruption scandal in recent years, the newspaper said.
Li Huanzheng, secretary of the Communist Party's provincial discipline committee, said the problem exposed by the scandal was "shocking".
He called for "strict self-discipline, self-respect, self-examination...and vigilance", the newspaper said.
Corruption, virtually eliminated in the years after the puritan communists came to power in 1949, has staged a comeback in the past two decades as economic reforms have eroded socialist ethics.
Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin has declared war on corruption, warning that the centuries-old scourge was like a virus that threatened the party's five-decade-old grip on power.
